entry.title: Splasher v0.0.9
entry.content:
# Splasher Archipelago (**v.0.0.9**) -- Checkpoint Sanity
**This version requires to update the APWorld accordingly**
**Don't forget to update your asset files**
## Highlights
### Checkpoint Sanity
A new randomization layer has been added : checkpoints sanity. When enabled, each checkpoint in the game becomes a location and, optionally, needs a corresponding *item* to be triggered. Checkpoints items have different levels of relevance depending on your (*CheckpointSanity*) option :
- `useful` : the item allows its checkpoint to save the level progression (essence, position). Upon dying, the player respawns to the farthest **unlocked** checkpoint. - `progression` : the item also allows to send uncollected splashers. With this option checkpoint items may appear in a seed's logic, although it is currently somewhat limited because level exits are not yet gated by items (this will be worked on in the next version).
Checkpoint items, if enabled, can be added in the pool as : - **individual** items (one per checkpoint) - **level pack** items (one per level, unlocking all checkpoints in it) - **zone pack** items (one per zone, unlocking all checkpoints in it)
### In-game item feedback
A feature that I should've implemented way earlier, but the game finally shows a pop-up message when you receive an item. How this is implemented is quite similar to [Celeste Open World](https://archipelago.gg/games/Celeste%20(Open%20World)/info/en) : a pop-up appears for a few seconds on the top-center of your screen, lasting for a few seconds (defaults to 5s, can be adjusted in `connection.yaml`).
## Additional features
- Added an option to instantly collect splashers (without reaching a checkpoint). This is a **seed** option (not overridable in `connection.yaml`) because it affects the logic the randomizer. - You can know teleport towards the next checkpoint (if that checkpoint is unlocked), reducing runbacks.

# Fixes - Crash / blackscreen when save-quitting while AP menu is open - Kaleidoscope now correctly gives 3 card rewards from other characters (instead of 0, 1, 2 cards depending on your unlocked characters) - Hopefully fix the issue when connecting to an older APworld and not sending any checks (in my testing it didn't work for some reason and then worked when i restart - I would not be surprised if it showed up again - Fix the behaviour where Silver Crucible, Silken Tress etc did not work correctly - they now consume upon viewing a Card Reward for the first time - opposes base game behaviour - One of the above hopefully fixes the ancient relics breaking (I didn't notice them breaking in my testing) - Multiplayer scroll being able to be selected as a Neow Relic and it breaking (in Anytime mode)

## Pre-Requisites
- **Your host MUST use Archipelago Client v0.6.7+**. - This version of the mod is intended to be used for **v0.107.1** of Slay the Spire II - While we have experimental support for the public beta branch **v0.111.0**, we recommend **the "Default Public/Main Version"** of the game to most players. Since the beta branch is updated more frequently and is more volatile, it's less likely to be bug-free. Please use it at your own risk. However numerous players have used it just fine, @Terairk is the maintainer for this and he mostly develops here. - We will do our best to keep up with game updates as they release, so please be patient when encountering issues.
## Installing the Mod from Steam Workshop (Recommended)
1. Ensure that you have [RitsuLib](https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3747602295) installed. The easiest way to obtain it is from Steam Workshop. 2. Subscribe to the [Slay the Spire II Archipelago Client](https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3748826296) on Steam Workshop. 3. Make sure that any other unnecessary mods are turned off, unless you're trying to use a specific modded character for your Archipelago session. 4. Start the game
## Manually Installing the Mod from GitHub
1. Ensure that you have [RitsuLib](https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3747602295) installed. The easiest way to obtain it is from Steam Workshop. 2. Download the "Archipelago.zip" from the [Releases](https://github.com/dlueben1/Slay-the-Spire-2-Archipelago/releases/latest) section of the Repo 3. Go to your Slay the Spire II directory (In Steam, click "Browse Local Files") 4. If a folder called `mods` does not exist, create it 5. Copy the `Archipelago.zip` into `mods`. Then click `extract all` on your favourite ZIP tool.
- If you've done this step correctly, your directory structure should look like this: `/<slay-the-spire-2-local-files>/mods/Archipelago/` and the contents of that folder should be a bunch of `.dll` files and a `.pck` file (there may be more files too, please don't touch anything in this folder)
6. Start the game
### Additional Steps for **Hosts**
7. Download `spire2.apworld` 8. Open your Archipelago Launcher 9. Click "Install APWorld" 10. Select `spire2.apworld` in the file dialog that pops up 11. **Restart the Archipelago Launcher** 12. Now you should be able to properly host/generate an Archipelago Session with StS 2
- If you want to use `archipelago.gg` to host the game, generate it locally first following the steps above, then upload the `.zip` file from the `output` folder in your Archipelago installation
> [!IMPORTANT] > You need to use Archipelago Version 0.6.7+ and CANNOT use earlier versions of Archipelago with this mod!

entry.title: Harry Potter 2 PC v2.11.0
entry.content:
# HP2PC_AP v2.11.0 Every link is now a command you can flip mid-run, auto-launch only fires when you ask for it, and Hold Shift runs faster. Plus an eleventh Diffindo plant pot and four logic corrections.
### New - **Turn each link on or off during a run.** `/ringlink`, `/traplink` and `/deathlink` each take `on`, `off` or `seed`, and a bare command flips the current state. Your choice beats the seed setting on every reconnect, so dropping and rejoining keeps it. - **`/autoplay` overrides auto-launch for the client session.** It takes `on` or `off`, and a bare `/autoplay` flips it. Handy when you want one session to behave differently from your `auto_launch_game` setting.
### Changed - **Auto-launch only fires on connects you made.** The Connect button, `/connect` and the startup connect arm the launch. A reconnect the client makes by itself after a dropped connection never launches. The game counts as already up when it is bridged or a `Game.exe` is visible, so closing the game at the launcher page no longer wedges auto-launch for the rest of the session. A skipped launch says so and points you at `/play`. - **Hold Shift now caps at 330 units per second**, up from 315. The cap scales off the live ground speed, so a boost the game gives you on its own still stacks on top. - **Blocker hints get a reach per site.** The Great Hall gate drops to 150 units and the Spongify and Skurge doorways to 100, about contact range, so those three stop announcing themselves from across the room. Everything else keeps the 500 unit reach.
### Fixed - **A timed trap can no longer expire mid-climb.** Reducio and Engorgio rebuild Harry's collision cylinder when they run out, which corrupted it if he was on a ledge at the time. Expiry now waits until he is standing or walking. Leaving the level still ends the trap immediately. - **A container the engine refuses to swap comes back.** A rejected spawn retries through the engine's own outward search and slides back to the saved spot. A spot that still refuses gets the stock container instead of an empty gap.
### Logic and content changes - **Diffindo Challenge has an eleventh plant pot.** The pot set into a wall sconce is a check again, as Plant Pot 8. The pots that were 8, 9 and 10 are now 9, 10 and 11, each keeping its own check. - **Gryffindor Challenge Cauldron 2** now needs **Alohomora** on top of (Diffindo or Running) + Spongify + Flipendo. Cauldron 1 is unchanged. - **Quidditch match 5** no longer needs **Spongify**. Match 6 unlocks at a later game state, past the Spongify lesson, so only match 6 carries the spell. - **Forbidden Forest Secret 4 and Card Scamander** now need **Flipendo**. Both need it to reach. - **Chamber of Secrets Wiggentree Bark Jar 1 and Flobberworm Mucous Jar 1** now need **Diffindo**. Both sit behind a cut.
## Poptracker 1.0.8
### Changed - Access rules regenerated for the Cauldron 2, Quidditch match 5, Forbidden Forest and Chamber of Secrets gates. - Diffindo Challenge Plant Pot 11 added, and the plant pot pins retargeted so each pin follows its pot rather than its number.

entry.title: Final Fantasy VIII v0.4.0
entry.content:
> ## ⚠️ Stability note > v0.4.0 carries the **early-Ragnarok** work (Vehicle Unlocks / Vehicle Gates), which manipulates the game's world map in ways no previous release did. It has been through one live test session, not a full playthrough, so expect rough edges: a ship parked somewhere odd, a spawn that needs one more battle, a save made aboard behaving strangely. Both vehicle options are **off by default**, and the sphere changes are generation-only. **If you want the most stable experience for a long multiworld, use [v0.3.0](https://github.com/wilsonao/ff8_arch/releases/tag/v0.3.0)** and report anything you hit on v0.4.0.
## What's new in v0.4.0
- **Story Gates** (new option, default `normal`): the story is split into 18 beats and each beat's checks count as in logic only once you hold a rising ladder of GFs and unlock items. A default seed now opens about 60 checks (all Disc 1) and plays as 8-13 real spheres instead of 220 checks in one plateau. `tight` for about 25, `off` for the old shape. - **Travel hubs:** the world-map draw points of Centra, Trabia, Esthar, and the islands open with the Ragnarok item *or* the story beat that grants it. - **Vehicle Unlocks** (experimental, off): the Ragnarok item spawns the ship beside you after a battle or town exit, on any disc, and you keep it for the whole game. The Balamb Garden item was removed (a mobile Garden locks you out of Balamb Garden). - **Vehicle Gates** (experimental, off): the story's own Ragnarok is parked out at sea until the item arrives. - New **Staircase** preset; PopTracker pack 0.10.0 mirrors the beats, hubs, and ladder; `tools/sphere_report.py` for measuring sphere shape.
## Install
1. Archipelago **Launcher** → **Install APWorld** → pick `ff8.apworld` (or copy it into `custom_worlds/`), then restart the Launcher. 2. Optional: drop `ff8_ap_tracker.zip` into PopTracker's `packs/` folder. 3. Optional: `ff8_visual_tracker.zip` is a map preset for the [Archipelago Visual Tracker](https://github.com/Wakamu/Archipelago/releases/latest) — see **Visual Tracker** below.
### Visual Tracker
`ff8_visual_tracker.zip` pins every FF8 check on clickable world / extras / GF-ability maps inside the Archipelago Visual Tracker client. To use it:
1. Install [Universal Tracker](https://github.com/FarisTheAncient/Archipelago/releases?q=Tracker) (`tracker.apworld`) and [`visualtracker.apworld`](https://github.com/Wakamu/Archipelago/releases/latest) via **Launcher → Install APWorld**, then restart the Launcher. 2. Copy `ff8_visual_tracker.zip` into the `visual_packs/` folder of your Archipelago install (create it next to `custom_worlds/` if missing). Do **not** unzip it. 3. Launcher → **Visual Tracker**, connect to your server/slot; the FF8 preset is picked up automatically.
Visual Tracker support grew out of a community map layout contributed by **caedesender** (Discord) — thank you!
Requires Archipelago 0.6.7+ and *Final Fantasy VIII* Steam 2013 (`FF8_EN.exe`). Setup guide: the **Final Fantasy VIII** page on your WebHost, or the [Player Guide](https://github.com/wilsonao/ff8_arch/blob/main/docs/player-guide.md).
## What's Changed * v0.4.0: story-beat sphere gating, travel hubs, early Ragnarok by @wilsonao in https://github.com/wilsonao/ff8_arch/pull/1
## New Contributors * @wilsonao made their first contribution in https://github.com/wilsonao/ff8_arch/pull/1
**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/wilsonao/ff8_arch/compare/v0.3.0...v0.4.0

entry.title: Team Fortress 2 Mann vs Machine v1.12.0r2
entry.content: ## Changes Traps, a medal on every mission clear, a Grappling Hook the multiworld can hand you, maps that download over HTTP, thirty more community missions, and a long pass over the weapon buffs from Cowser's sheet and kelly-cs's issues. Bots at 2.52.3. The settings screen says what it did with a Save and where it put the file, and a save stops ending the mission you are four waves into. ### The run - **Traps.** A `trap_percentage` option puts traps in the pool, one percent by default and zero for none. The one that exists soaks the whole team in Jarate: ten seconds of 35% more damage taken and no crits, bots included. It belongs to the multiworld like any other item, so it is another player opening a chest that does it to you. One that arrives between waves waits for the next one: Jarate on a team standing at the upgrade station is no trap at all. - **Australium Medals.** `medal_on_clear`, off by default, locks a medal onto every mission clear and takes those checks out of the pool. Both goals read them: Final Boss asks for the goal mission's own, missionsanity counts them. - **The Grappling Hook.** Turn on `server_settings` in your YAML and the multiworld can hand your team Mannpower's hook for the rest of the run. It is useful, never progression: no wave needs it. - A `community_missions` option keeps every community mission out of a run in one line, instead of naming each in `excluded_missions`. - Thirty community missions that play on a Valve map are on the lists. Every mission in the catalogue named one of its own community maps, so Moonlight's Trouble in Mann Town on Coaltown and Manntenance on Mannworks were in the downloaded assets and on no list. They need their pack for the population file and nothing else. A run that keeps every mission draws from 112 at the normal floor instead of 82, and the defaults do not move: community missions still start excluded. Reported by Glitch. - Community missions can name a server mod they need. The Docker image carries SigMod and loads it with `SRCDS_MODS=sigsegv-mvm`; the seed's `server_mods` option draws those missions only for a server that has it. The Windows launcher shows them locked: SigMod has no Windows build. - Wicked Wizardry and Fiefdom Fiasco on Frostwynd are Medieval missions: the map keeps only melee and medieval-era weapons, so most weapon slot unlocks do nothing there. The launcher says so where you pick missions for the pool, where you choose the starting mission, and on the session list, so a run does not walk into one by surprise. By kelly-cs. - A server that restarts goes back to the wave the team had reached. The bridge writes the wave down as checks come in, and the plugin reloads the mission and jumps forward, never back, when the server comes up again. A crash cost the team every wave it had cleared. - A run that crossed the 1.10 upgrade had every mission it had cleared read as "collected", and a missionsanity goal counted none of them. The old state file could not say which checks were yours, and they all were. kelly-cs's run. - The bridge no longer drops the room every second in a multiworld with many games. It asked for every game's item names at once and the reply was too big to read, so nothing you checked ever reached the room. EMann's bundle showed it fifty-nine times. - Test mode draws its missions at random from the pool, the way a real seed does. It took the first ones in the settings list, which looked like a randomizer that does not randomize. ### Weapon buffs - The run's buffs are yours and not the station's. Refunding an upgrade used to take them, and they came back as purchased, infinitely refundable upgrade levels that stacked again on each refund. They are held apart from MvM's shopping now and survive refunds, wave transitions and loadout changes. - The upgrade station no longer opens the buff window by itself. That window took the number keys, which are your weapon slots, for twenty seconds. The station lists your loadout's buffs in chat, and `!ap buffs` opens the window when you want it. - Explode on ignite is gone from the pool: on a minigun it ended a wave on its own. - Über on hit is a Medic buff. It used to be offered on mediguns only, which never land a hit, so it did nothing wherever it fell. It is on his syringe guns, his saws and the Crusader's Crossbow now: 1% a syringe, because they land far faster, and 5% everywhere else. - Ninety-six buff and weapon pairs that did nothing are out of the pool, from Cowser's sheet: accuracy on weapons with no spread, reload and clip buffs on weapons with no clip, kill buffs on the two jumpers, fire rate on sniper rifles, and the like. Existing seeds keep their ids. - Eight pairs came in from the same sheet. A thrown jar counts as a hit, so Jarate and Mad Milk draw ignite and heal on hit. The Gas Passer never fires and still gets kills through its afterburn, so it draws the on-kill buffs. - Projectile penetration is no longer offered on explosives: a rocket that penetrates does not explode where it was aimed. Armor piercing is a knife buff only, since the game reads it on backstabs and nowhere else. - Bleed lands one stack per enemy instead of one per hit, which made a syringe gun a wave-ender. Melee fire rate stops at +50%: past it the swing outran its own animation and hit nothing. - "No self-inflicted blast damage" and rocket-jump protection work on rocket, grenade and stickybomb launchers, and zero self-damage keeps the explosion and the blast-jump push. The game reads both on the player, not the weapon, so the buff on the weapon never reached them. - Bleed, milk, Jarate and the marks land on a direct hit with the jar itself. - A locked weapon slot takes the wearable in it too. A Demoman with a locked secondary charged with a shield, and one with a locked primary kept the boots and held nothing. Gunboats, Mantreads, the Razorback and the other slot-filling wearables follow the same rule. - Linux servers get the extra arrows and flares. The projectile-count fanout had Windows gamedata only, so a Docker server logged both fanouts disabled and every extra bolt was a plain clone. - Extra Crusader's Crossbow bolts heal. The fanout built them as plain arrows, which hurt a robot and do nothing for a teammate. They now come off the game's own arrow factory with their launcher set, so a bolt that reaches a teammate heals him, penetration carries over, and the weapon still fires one sound however many bolts leave it. By kelly-cs. - Heal on hit and speed boost on hit work on Jarate and Mad Milk. The game reads both off a weapon attack, and a jar splash is not one, so a soaked robot gave the thrower nothing. The plugin pays them now, once per soaked enemy. - The on-kill buffs credit the weapon that killed, not the one in hand. A robot that burned down after the Pyro put the Gas Passer away paid the flamethrower's buffs, or nothing. - `sm_ap_buff_slot` puts a test buff on a holstered weapon, a shield or a watch, and `tf2ap_buffs_for_defender_bots` lets the bots carry the run's buffs so a buff can be measured on a server with no player. - Movement speed, jump height and health regeneration are passive. They used to work only while the weapon that carried them was out, which is not how MvM's own class upgrades read; a Scout who rolls movement speed on his bat is faster with the scattergun in his hands too, and two weapons carrying the same buff add up. - Recharge speed is off the Gas Passer. It fills the item meter and the buff scales the effect bar, which is a different meter, so it never reached it. - The Flying Guillotine no longer draws clip size, reserve ammo or reload speed. It recharges, so it holds no rounds for any of them to act on. - A server where no buff applies at all says why in its log. The plugin hangs the buffs off an attribute provider it attaches through VScript, because TF2Utils' equip offset is stale on current Windows TF2, and a server with no VScript VM refuses that input. The refusal was dropped and came back a step later as the provider not providing attributes, which is a symptom no debug bundle could explain. Nine of those lines in four minutes sat behind Likai's screenshot. ### Balancing - Robot health scaling works, and holds. Setting it above 100% left the robots at the mission's health and setting it below moved nothing: the number was written somewhere the game recomputes a moment later. It is a straight multiplier now, 10% to 1000%, applied after the game finishes building the robot, read back, and the server log says what each robot ended up worth. ### Getting a server up - The server hands out maps over HTTP from the machine it runs on, so a friend joining without a community map downloads it instead of watching Transmission reach the end and start over. On the local network there is nothing to set up. A friend joining from outside needs the download port forwarded and your public address in `SRCDS_DOWNLOADURL`, or a Tailscale Funnel: the launcher publishes the download through it when you have one, on Windows and Linux and with the Compose stack. Without either they fall back to the old transfer. - The launcher says in its log when a newer release is out, with the link. It still does not replace itself: download the new exe and run it. - A server whose Metamod or SourceMod went missing is repaired on the next start instead of playing stock Mann vs Machine with every setting ignored, and a debug bundle says so when it happened. - The Docker server plays the randomiser again. The image shipped without the plugin's gamedata, so the plugin refused to load and the server came up as plain Mann vs Machine with nothing saying so. - The Docker server writes its player file with the same code as the launcher, so both carry the reward importance options and the same defaults. `MVM_COMMUNITY_MISSIONS` reaches the launcher's settings too. - The game server starts with `-debug`, so a crash leaves a stack in `debug.log` even when Breakpad never started, and the bundle carries it. Two bundles arrived with an access violation and nothing naming the function. - A debug bundle only carries the game server's own crash dumps, not every program's on the machine. Two bundles carried GameBar and a Tony Hawk game. - The community mission installer skips the missions a pack cannot support. ### The launcher - An **Unlocks** tab, window and terminal, lists what the multiworld has handed the run: classes, weapon slots, missions and weapon buffs, with the level a repeated buff reached. - The install folder is a setting, with Browse beside it, instead of a choice the installer screen made once and never offered again. Changing it does not move what is already downloaded, and the help says so. - **Show the settings file** opens the folder holding `config.json`, which is under the OS config directory and not in the install folder. Two players went looking for it in the install folder, found nothing, and concluded that nothing had saved. - A Save that is refused says so where you are looking: a message box, and the page holding the reason. A refusal used to be a small label beside a box on another tab, so a player could set a login token three times over while the room address two pages away was what stopped every one of them. Every refusal is in the log now as well, so a debug bundle carries it. - A failed write keeps the screen up with your answers on it and names the path it could not write. - Save asks the room whether it is listening, and says which of "live", "not there" or "did not answer" it got. None of the three refuses the save: a room you have not made yet is not a mistake. Start used to be where you found out, with "AP_PORT is not set", and one player spent seventeen minutes on that. - The mission count you may ask for is the number the seed can actually draw. The ceiling counted every mission in the catalogue, including the community ones a fresh settings file leaves out and any needing a server mod you do not load, so the tier rows offered 82 missions at the normal floor where the run held 29. Both numbers now count what the generator counts, and the generator says in its log when the pool is smaller than the ask. Reported by [-SAM-]. - The settings window is laid out like a settings window again. Moving the rows into one declaration flattened it: the Bots page became one list of thirty-nine rows where it had been four sub-tabs, every button took a line with its own name in the label column beside it, Debug logs, Repair and Reset settings left the bottom bar for a page, and a page of three settings spread its rows down the window instead of leaving the space at the bottom. The window nests, groups and lays out again: Bots holds Team, Classes, Looks and Loadouts; the seats and the classes sit two to a line; buttons share a line; numbers are the width of a number rather than of the window; and the three buttons that are about the launcher are along the bottom where they were. - SourceMod's one automatic restart waits for the settings window to close. The updater fetches gamedata and asks for a restart whenever it likes, so the server came round in the middle of an edit and looked like the edit had done it: Sirknobbles reported changing the bot team as restarting the server, but only when the window had been open long enough. A save that restarts anyway loads the new gamedata itself. - A save restarts the server only for a setting the server reads at startup. Saving a mission count ended the mission the team was four waves into and brought the server back exactly as it was. A **Restart on save** tick sits beside Save and shows only when what is on screen would need one, never with the server down, so a lineup changed between waves costs the run nothing. Reported by Likai. - A run of nothing but community missions has missions again. The community switch was absent from every settings file written before the option existed, so it loaded as off, and no screen had a row to turn it back on once it was the field that empties the pool. It has one on the Missions page, and a community mission's Compatibility column reads "community missions are off" while the switch is, so the table stops looking full over an empty pool. Reported by Peppy. - A run selection the launcher refuses is reported as refused. The button dropped the error naming the empty pool and printed "Selection is valid: 0 eligible mission(s) provide 0 checks for 0 unlocks" over it. From Peppy's screenshot. - The mission table sorts on its headers, and a row it was told about redraws. The "In the pool" column kept its old answer until the mouse passed over the line, and a tick the launcher had refused was drawn as taken. The headers looked pressable and did nothing, which with eighty-five missions makes finding one a nightmare. The table opens sorted by mission name. Reported by EZKSupernova. - The settings window opens on a number saved outside the bounds it has now. The mission pool can shrink under a count already saved, and the window refuses to build at all for one number box starting outside its range, so nothing opened. The stale value sits on the nearest bound, where you can see it and save it. By kelly-cs. - Terminal tabs that list more than fits scroll, and the last line counts what is off the screen. The Unlocks and Bot Switcher lists were cut at the body height and said nothing about the rest. - `-web` opts into an experimental browser interface, the same screens on Windows and Linux, served on loopback by the launcher itself. The window and the terminal interface stay the defaults until a later cutover. By kelly-cs. ### The bots The mod moves from 2.39.0 to 2.52.3. - The medic answers a player who calls for him. A human pressed the call and the bot medic carried on healing whichever bot it had picked; reported by Cowser and by Peppy. Measured with a stand-in player calling on Decoy: the caller held the beam up to a quarter of the time against 2% before, every wave cleared either way. - The engineer's break is a plan, not a walk. Every engineer claims his four spots before anybody moves, jumps to each rather than walking, and never builds on another engineer's ground. On Decoy with two engineers the teleporter entrance stands at 21 to 30 seconds of the break against 37 to 45, and the exit at 26 to 38 against 50 to 58. The cost is on the record: the wrench is what applies a level, and an engineer who jumps swings it less, so the sentry sits at level three in 76% of samples rather than 85%. - Two engineers who pick the same nest no longer land inside each other. The sentry was the one building whose jump onto its spot skipped the check for room to stand, so a pair holding one nest were put on the same coordinate and neither could move until the stuck recovery threw one of them out. Reported by Cowser on Mannworks, where five engineers share four nest spots and the pair spent the whole break wedged with no sentry between them. - A teleporter exit puts you down on a side with ground beside it. The exit ring never looked down, so a player taking the teleporter could land where the engineer never stood. - A bot's loadout slot is emptied only for an item the game can give. A Heavy joined RED on Rottenburg with no weapon at all. - Halloween cosmetics are out of the bots' hat pool. The game refuses to attach a holiday item out of season, and the refusal threw an error that cost the bot the rest of its cosmetics. - A bot moved out of spawn is put where a standing player fits. The recovery teleported onto anything and asked for a route in the same tick. - Five map spots stand on the ground. Four nest and dispenser spots on Mannhattan and Mannworks sat in holes beside the mesh, and Rottenburg's fourth sniper spot was written 213 units above it, so every side was refused. - A bot taking a seat no longer inherits the last bot's answers: the health, ammo and revive searches around where the previous bot stood cleared with the seat, so a new bot stops walking to a pack it cannot reach. - The server no longer crashes on a map change after a custom loadout file was loaded. Two handles the mod had closed were read back after the change. - The final wave's send-off is a taunt. The last wave neither danced nor kicked. Bigrock's rock-top nest and teleporter spots are still built at the foot of the rock: the engineer cannot climb, and the building goes where he stands. Open. ## Windows Download **`tf2ap.exe`** above. Run it. It installs everything else. Windows will warn you, and it is a false positive. The exe unpacks archives and starts a game server without a code signature, which looks like a virus to a scanner. Click **More info**, then **Run anyway**, or check it below first. [Full guide](https://m-this.github.io/tf2-archipelago/en/setup/install-windows.html) ## Linux Download **`tf2ap-linux-amd64`**. Run it. It installs everything else. ```sh chmod +x tf2ap-linux-amd64 ./tf2ap-linux-amd64 ``` [Full guide](https://m-this.github.io/tf2-archipelago/en/setup/install-linux.html) ## Docker Download **`compose.yaml`** and **`.env.example`**: ```sh mkdir mann-vs-archipelago && cd mann-vs-archipelago base=https://github.com/m-this/tf2-archipelago/releases/latest/download curl -fsSLO "$base/compose.yaml" curl -fsSL -o .env "$base/.env.example" ``` Set `SRCDS_RCONPW` in `.env`, then: ```sh docker compose --profile seed run --rm seed # writes ./seed docker compose up -d ``` Upload the file from `seed/` at [archipelago.gg/uploads](https://archipelago.gg/uploads) and put the room's port into `AP_PORT`. [Full guide](https://m-this.github.io/tf2-archipelago/en/setup/install.html) ## Other assets | File | For | | --- | --- | | `tf2_mvm.apworld` | The official Archipelago app. | | `tf2_archipelago.smx` | A SourceMod server the launcher and compose file don't manage. | | `tf2-defender-bots.zip` | The bots for that same server. Unzip into `tf/`. | | `meta.json`, `items.json`, `missions.json` | The item and check tables, for reference. | ## Checking what you downloaded **`SHA256SUMS`** is attached to this release. It holds the hash of every file here, computed by the workflow that built them. ```powershell Get-FileHash tf2ap.exe -Algorithm SHA256 # Windows ``` ```sh sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS --ignore-missing # Linux ``` Each binary carries a signed record of the commit and the workflow that built it: ```sh gh attestation verify tf2ap.exe --repo m-this/tf2-archipelago ``` The binaries are scanned on VirusTotal, and the reports are linked at the end of these notes. Expect a few heuristic detections and no named malware family. The source is all in the repository, and `make launcher` rebuilds the exe on your own machine. ## Code signing policy Free code signing for open source projects, provided by [SignPath.org](https://signpath.org), with a certificate from the [SignPath Foundation](https://signpath.org). > [!WARNING] > The application is open, not granted. Nothing is signed yet: `tf2ap.exe` ships > unsigned, and Windows warns about it until that changes. ## What's Changed * fix(plugin): isolate Archipelago buffs from MvM upgrades / fix a refund bug related to it by @kelly-cs in https://github.com/m-this/tf2-archipelago/pull/7 * fix(ci): clear baseline Go checks by @kelly-cs in https://github.com/m-this/tf2-archipelago/pull/14 * fix(bridge): fix checks not sending to the archipelago server / retry without needing to restart server by @kelly-cs in https://github.com/m-this/tf2-archipelago/pull/11 * fix(installer): filter unsupported community missions by @kelly-cs in https://github.com/m-this/tf2-archipelago/pull/10 * feat(bots): scale robot maximum health by @kelly-cs in https://github.com/m-this/tf2-archipelago/pull/13 * fix(plugin): apply substance buffs correctly w/ all weapons by @kelly-cs in https://github.com/m-this/tf2-archipelago/pull/9 * fix(plugin): restore active weapon health regeneration by @kelly-cs in https://github.com/m-this/tf2-archipelago/pull/8 * fix(bots): take the robot health fix from the module, not from a patch by @m-this in https://github.com/m-this/tf2-archipelago/pull/29 * feat(community): let a mission require a server mod by @m-this in https://github.com/m-this/tf2-archipelago/pull/28 * feat(server): FastDL from the machine that runs the game by @m-this in https://github.com/m-this/tf2-archipelago/pull/27 * fix(plugin): preserve self-blast jumps and explosions by @kelly-cs in https://github.com/m-this/tf2-archipelago/pull/31 * feat(launcher): publish FastDL with Tailscale Funnel by @kelly-cs in https://github.com/m-this/tf2-archipelago/pull/30 * feat(launcher): label medieval-loadout missions by @kelly-cs in https://github.com/m-this/tf2-archipelago/pull/12 * fix(plugin): heal teammates with extra Crossbow bolts by @kelly-cs in https://github.com/m-this/tf2-archipelago/pull/34 * fix(plugin): make ammo on hit reliable by @kelly-cs in https://github.com/m-this/tf2-archipelago/pull/35 * feat(plugin): add stomp weapon buffs by @kelly-cs in https://github.com/m-this/tf2-archipelago/pull/36 * fix(plugin): apply stomp kill effects by @kelly-cs in https://github.com/m-this/tf2-archipelago/pull/37 * fix(plugin): extend projectile destruction to guns by @kelly-cs in entry.title: Yakuza Gaiden v0.6.0r2
entry.content:
## Update notes, and goals for the next build
First a small aside, I name the builds based all around the myth of the carp climbing the waterfall to become a dragon, because c'mon this is a yakuza randomizer! We started with varieties of fish pre AP integration, then moved to monstrous fish, or dragon fish, since. And on release will likely move to dragon names! This one is named Akuru, which is named after a massive sea monster fish that could eat boats, symbolizing how crazy the bloat became on this build, as it truly became monstrous!
Massive release, likely to be met with massive bugs, I swear the next builds will be smaller, and more focused on optimizations and bug fixes over new features, rather than waiting till the next massive feature release before fixing small issues.
This build focuses on Akame tasks, logic changes, bug fixes, and some new features tied to requests from the awesome beta testing you all have done!
The goal with the following major release will be focused on clean up and QoL features over new content. So consider this the "Last Main Feature" build for adding checks and complex features for at least some chunk of time. The goal for 0.8.0 is to look into trackers, visual displays of items when received, optimizations and code cleanup, and maybe some fun features like deathlink if time allows. And set us up well for the final pre 1.0.0 release which would mark my satisfaction and completion with the randomizer.
To clarify, there will likely be a handful of post 1.0.0 changes as you would expect, or as I come up with new ideas. But that's when I can consider it at least "finished" for what that's worth. And that's still quite a ways away.
That being said, there's no better time to play then now! Every build gets a bit more efficient, clean, and fun. So like always, if you test it out and have an issue, please reach out to me either through discord, submitting an issue through Github, or make a post on the AP Afterdark page for Gaiden.
Anyway, here are the patch notes!
## Yakuza Gaiden randomizer Version 0.7.0 (Akuru)
- Akame Tasks now give checks! This can be adjusted using options to remove individual types of Akame Tasks if you want to avoid certain ones. Akame Tasks are split between: 1. Fetch: Tasks where you must provide an item to the person 3. Trial: Tasks where you must perform well at a certain game, or navigate and do some unique action 4. Photo: Tasks where you take a photograph of the requested item 5. Combat: Tasks where you defend the recipient or open an area blocked off to you 6. Outift: Tasks where Kiryu must dress the part to receive the reward
- Story moments now also present checks. Defeating notable fights, or completing a dungeon will provide a check to the player now to incentivize progression more than just as a way to finish the game. More of these may be added/deactivated per testing. - Hints have been added to shops and Akame Tasks. Purchasing an item from a store will hint the store for later quick reference, examining an Akame Task in the city that you cannot finish from just talking to them, will also hint that item to help you know if its worth pursuing. This feature has not been extensively tested, so please let me know if any locations fail to hint when you do not have the item in your inventory! - Pocket Circuit cars now contain 5 checks when acquired! This causes each pocket circuit car to be MUCH more valuable as a key item, as each on may contain the crucial parts you may need to finish your races! the remaining parts are still scattered across the worlds so this merely cuts down the amount of pocket circuit parts spread between worlds. - New goals and wincons. Added Defeat Shishido, and Defeat Pocket Circuit Owner Rival Race to the goal list alongside the existing Golden ball wincons. Multiple wincons can now be set at once! and all goals will need to be met to send the goal complete alert, this also has full go mode support too to let you know when its time! - Substories have checks! Completing a Substory now gives 1 check. Currently this is all but the Amon sub story, or the colosseum specific ones with the Kings. - Progressive wires now go up to the max possible in each region, in case you wanted to do just that! - All wires have been (likely) found! Giving us a total of 39 sotenbori, 29 Yokohama, and 19 colosseum - Clothing prices have been removed, all cosmetics are now free, requiring just the item to be sent to you, let those toes out without dropping 1 million yen! - South Poppo has been renamed to West Poppo to avoid confusion, Park Poppo remains as such - Your unique seed is actually unique now. Before if two Gaidens were in the same multiworld, all equipment would randomize the same stats + abilities. This has been changed to a per slot version of the seed now to avoid this hiccup. - swap invalid setting for YAML. If settings are invalid we now have backend validations in place to clean up and fix the yaml before run time. This should fix all min/max problems people were running into, and more importantly allow you to randomize all settings! - Shop keys are now separated into Shop Key and Minigame Key options. This allows you to lock one but not the other if preferred! - Unused key items are removed from the pool (for sure this time), for example if shop keys are on, but consumable shops are off, the consumable shop keys will not be included. - Shigano gains more checks... kind of? Shigano now contains a handful of infinite purchasable items that are required for Akame Tasks, and Akame Fetch tasks are only in logic if Shigano is open to purchase. The randomizer *should* give you the items you need within the pool, but this is a catch all to prevent those emergency bento boxes softlocking you. - Many bug fixes to edge case scenarios for saving and loading with AP items being sent. - Akame should no longer remove your shop keys if given a smoke - Multiple Prompt and console changes to hopefully clear up any confusion (for example /slot is now allowed alongside slot, there will likely be even more changes coming).

entry.title: Peggle Deluxe v2.0.0
entry.content: This is a major feature release that also includes improvements. **This release is NOT compatible with games generated on the previous version.** - **Feature:** In-Game Level Locking - **Feature:** In-Game Master Locking - **Feature:** Progressive Fever Meter Threshold items have been completely replaced by level-specific Progressive Orange Pegs items, leading to more interesting and layered progression, as well as requiring a bit more skill for the early game phase - **Feature:** Fever mode no longer starts upon hitting the last orange peg when you have less than 25 orange pegs on a given level which should lessen confusion around level clear locations, as well as allowing easier chasing of full clears - **Feature:** Purple Pegs are now unlockable by level - **Feature:** Each Peggle Master now has their own set of Progressive Green Pegs items, creating opportunities for suboptimal masters to now be optimal to play under certain circumstances - **Improvement:** Starting level count increased from 1 to 3 - **Improvement:** Starting ball count is now set through a custom code patch instead of directly setting the memory value, meaning that the Ball-O-Tron will now always display the correct amount of balls - **Improvement:** Getting the required quantity of Gold Pegs is now all that's needed to access and clear the final level. No extra items to chase - **Improvement:** Added 3 extra copies of Progressive Starting Ball Increase and 1 extra copy of each Progressive Orange Pegs variant to allow for less restrictive progression and reaching the cap faster - **Improvement:** Slightly reworked logic, mainly around fever meter multipliers - **Improvement:** Custom client tab has been updated to reflect the new features _No new YAML options. Minimum level count is now 15 to make room for all the new items_ The implementation now has proper [documentation](https://github.com/SerpentAI/Archipelago/blob/peggle/worlds/peggle_deluxe/docs/en_Peggle_Deluxe.md) and a [setup guide](https://github.com/SerpentAI/Archipelago/blob/peggle/worlds/peggle_deluxe/docs/setup_en.md)

entry.title: ARK Survival Evolved v1.0.0r5
entry.content:
## Release Notes
1. **Fjordur is here**.
2. Midgard, Asgard, Jotunheim, and Vanaheim occupy the same world space at different elevations, so exploration regions now include altitude bands.
**81 exploration checks total:** - Midgard: 38 - Asgard: 20 - Vanaheim: 14 - Jotunheim: 9
3. **All 200 Fjordur Runes are now checks.** Runes are treated as Explorer Notes under the hood, so collecting one just works. Cave, underwater, and wyvern trench runes are gated behind the gear actually needed to reach them. The 45 runes in Asgard, Jotunheim, and Vanaheim currently contain filler only.
4. **The Norse bosses are now supported as goals.** Beyla, Hati & Sköll, and Steinbjörn lead into Fenrisúlfr. Boss kills are detected using the relic dropped by each fight instead of the boss corpse, so the kill still counts if you relog, another player gets the killing blow, or the corpse despawns. Hati & Sköll requires both relics.
5. **New goal setting:** choose any combination of bosses using a list.
```yaml goal: [broodmother, manticore, fenrisulfr] ```
`all_bosses` means every boss available across your selected maps. The default remains the four Island bosses.
**BREAKING CHANGE:** The following goal options no longer parse: - `all_bosses_all_maps` - `broodmother_megapithecus` - `broodmother_megapithecus_dragon`
Update your YAML accordingly.
6. **Fixed 32 engrams** that could previously be received but would never actually unlock. This includes Clay, Tent, Vessel, the full Adobe set, the Desert Cloth set, Wind Turbine, Thorny Dragon Saddle, and Rock Golem Saddle.
7. **Added 14 previously missing engrams:** Maewing, Velonasaur, Ravager, Amargasaurus, Roll Rat, Karkinos, Tropeognathus, Managarmr, and Magmasaur saddles, plus the full five-piece Hazard Suit. These saddles now correctly bundle with their associated tame when `bundle_saddles` is enabled. Previously, that setting did nothing for them.
8. **Unlock messages now explain why something unlocked.**
Example:
```text Explore: The Savage Heights (Asgard) unlocked for everyone on the server: Engram: ... ```
9. **No more trap floods from `!release` or `!collect`.** Bulk deliveries now skip traps, keep useful filler, and send a single notification in chat.
10. **Shared Slot + DeathLink now actually kills the entire server.** If one survivor dies, everyone dies. Previously, the death was sent to every other game in the multiworld while the survivors standing next to the corpse were left completely unaffected.
11. **51 dead-end cosmetics are now filler instead of useful items.** This includes signs, flags, furniture, elevators, pipes, trophies, and similar items that previously diluted the useful item pool. Actual gear remains useful.
12. **Added Mejoberry collection checks** and completed a broader food-tag pass.
13. **Datapackage updates:** - Engrams: 588 → 610 - Creatures: 127 → 142 - Exploration regions: 154 → 235 - Plugin: v177 → v187
14. **Generation sweep: 30/30 passing.** Configurations using `dossier_checks: 120` and `dossier_checks: 0` previously failed generation and now pass correctly.
---
## Tools
Attached are **Avocado's Launcher** and **Lurch's PopTracker**.
**Lurch's PopTracker:** https://github.com/lurch9229/Arkipelago-Poptracker/releases
**Avocado's Launcher:** https://github.com/aSoberAvocado/ARK-Ipelago-Evolved-Launcher/releases
I will be taking a break on adding new maps to the supported list as I am getting burnt out. I will be assisting Lurch with supporting the other released maps. I will continue working on bug fixes as they come up.

entry.title: Ocarina of Time v9.1.0r2
entry.content:
# OoT Randomizer APWorld v9.1.0 Full Release 2
This is a pretty well tested version by now. Generation fails still might happen on occasion, especially when using pre-completed dungeons.
## Changes: - Fixed a few left faulty grotto item ids that caused items not to show there in certain settings - Fixed lag with RetroArch connector and risk of item duplication on connect. - Removed fork mentions from template to comply with AP rules
Please note: Since OoT is currently not shipped as a bundled .apworld file, but unpacked by the core AP releases, you will have to delete the lib/worlds/oot folder first before adding this custom apworld. Even after deletion, the "Open Patch" Workflow in AP currently still starts the OoT Client, even if you deleted the world. So make sure you have the correct "Ocarina of Time Client" open that references the APWorld 9.1.0 after patching, or patch directly through the new Adjuster. If your client says "Archipelago Ocarina of Time Client 0.6.x" in the top bar with no info about the apworld version, you are using the old client.
